title: The Belief Record Schema
summary: Work through The Belief Record Schema.

blocks.md: This lesson covers the book's section on **The Belief Record Schema**. Read the excerpt, then test yourself below.

blocks.source: Vol IV, Spatial Memory, § The Belief Record Schema
blocks.md: The belief record introduced in a later section, the seventh record in the record chain, binds each state estimate to its capture epoch, coordinate frame, and error-growth law so that downstream controllers can catch a frozen transform, a chimeric frame chain, or a prediction that has outlived its slot tolerance. This schema unifies discrete tracked entities and continuous volumetric representations (a later section) under one set of time and error rules, serving both trajectory planning on the host and bounded local permission checks on real-time microcontrollers.

blocks.prompt: Think first: In two or three sentences, explain why Belief record matters for the system this section describes.
blocks.md: Compare your answer with the book's claim: Every spatial claim carries evidence, estimate, and publication epochs, and only a physical measurement advances the evidence epoch, so prediction and republishing must preserve it.

questions.q: The section **The Belief Record Schema** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: Space last seen free stays free only until an unseen agent could have entered it, so occluded free space shrinks at that agent's speed bound and blind crossings need site controls, not memory.
Every spatial claim carries evidence, estimate, and publication epochs, and only a physical measurement advances the evidence epoch, so prediction and republishing must preserve it.
A metric loop at camera rate keeps geometry current while foundation backbones update semantics on keyframes, and semantics never certify clearance.

A transform is a belief with its own epoch, so composing a stale camera-to-slot edge with current kinematics yields a pose the arm never occupied, and the lever arm, not clock resolution, sets the error.
